title: Traffic shepherding incident response & cross-region recovery playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create and validate an operational playbook for shepherding production traffic between regions and capacity tiers (hosted + dedicated). Includes deterministic steps for partial and full cross-region shifts, KV cache warming strategies, connection draining, canary criteria, automated rollback triggers, customer communication templates, and a short appendix for Private/VPC customers who manage their own routing.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook contains step-by-step commands for automated and manual traffic shifts between primary and secondary regions for both Hosted and Dedicated modes
Canary criteria defined: error rate < 0.5% and p95 latency within 20% of baseline for 5m window before increasing traffic by 25%
KV cache warming plan included to avoid cold-start regressions when shifting >10% traffic to a warmless node
Rollback procedures and circuit-breaker thresholds documented and tested in staging
Customer comms templates approved by Support and PM; one-page summary created for SEs
Related PRs merged and a smoke test dashboard (Grafana) created with alerting runbook links
runbook_steps: Triage: Confirm root cause and scope. Slack: #inc-ops, tag oncall and SRE lead. Create incident in PagerDuty if latency or error spikes cross SLOs.
Assess affected regions and capacity types (hosted/dedicated). Use /internal/region-health API and region-capacity dashboard to estimate time-to-stabilize.
Decide initial mitigation: advertise partial shift (10-25%) vs full failover. Choose based on customer impact and capacity headroom in target region.
For Hosted: execute traffic-shift job via routing-service CLI: `routingctl shift --from region-a --to region-b --percent 10 --wave 1`.
For Dedicated: coordinate with customer tenant owner and Dedicated capacity controller. If Dedicated has reserved pools, update tenant routing config and run balanced drain on source pools.

KV cache warming: launch controlled warmers (use `kv-warm --model <model> --region <target> --tokens 256 --qps 15`) tied to shift waves. Ensure warmers use representative prompts from stored prompt-sets.
Observe canary windows. If canary meets criteria, increase traffic by configured step (25%). If not, run rollback steps immediately.
Connection draining: reduce new connections to source region with a 60s drain window, preserve in-flight KV cache sessions for 90s to allow graceful completion.
If routing-service fails to apply changes or reports inconsistent state, escalate to runtime oncall and enable manual edge rule flip (CDN DNS TTL update) as an emergency fallback.
Post-shift validation: run synthetic smoke tests, verify token-level cost spikes, and check rate-limiters for per-customer quotas.
Customer communications: send initial notification to affected customers with expected window and next update cadence. Use the approved template (link in links).
Postmortem: capture timeline, root cause, mitigation effectiveness, and code/infra fixes required. Create PRD/bug tickets with owners and dates. Schedule postmortem review within 3 business days.
verification_checks: Grafana: p50/p95 latency, error rate, and request throughput by region. Ensure p95 within 20% of baseline and error rate < 0.5% for 5m.
Routing-service health: no failed change transactions and change-queue length < 50.
KV cache hit-rate in target region increases to expected steady-state within 10 minutes of shift.
No increase in token-cost anomalies per-token beyond 15% for shifted traffic within 30 minutes.
End-user-facing smoke tests pass (chat generation, streaming, embedding retrieval) for 5 different models representative of customers.

decisions: Prefer incremental trafffic waves with KV warming for model-heavy endpoints rather than abrupt full failover to minimize cold-cache regressions.
Use routing-service CLI as primary mechanism; manual CDN/DNS flip reserved as emergency fallback only.
Dedicated tenants that have active reserved pools must be consulted before automated shifts; default behavior is to propose an action and require tenant-owner approval.
Introduce synthetic warmers bound to shift jobs to avoid bringing unprimed GPUs into production traffic.
Add a post-shift smoke test suite as gating check before marking incident resolved.
next_steps: Merge PR that adds warmers to routingctl job orchestration (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6821).
Ship routing-service fix for stale CDN TTLs (ENG-19768) and add integration test covering edge caching behavior.
Coordinate with Support to rehearse customer comms template and publish a one-page SE guide.
Schedule a tabletop exercise with Dedicated and Private account managers to validate the tenant approval flow.
Add canary automation to bump traffic automatically when verification checks pass and to auto-rollback on violation.
notes_for_private_customers: Private deployments: we cannot shift traffic for you. Provide this playbook as a recommended cookbook and runbook snippets customers can paste into their routing automation.
Include an appendix with Terraform snippets to update VPC route tables and BGP community tags for on-prem failover scenarios.
Recommend customers enable the `redwood-warm` sidecar to pre-warm model state when they plan their own region shift.
Offer a runbook review session for enterprise customers on reserved Dedicated contracts (book via account team).
